key_decisions.ma_choice: Binary plus registered Gray pointers of ADDR_W+1 bits; DEPTH restricted to powers of 2; only the Gray copy crosses domains
key_decisions.plan_choice: Power-of-2 DEPTH with an elaboration assertion; ADDR_W+1-bit pointers; Gray value registered before the crossing
key_decisions.note: The spec says 'Gray pointers' and 'power of 2 OK', which effectively fixes this.

key_decisions.ma_choice: All flags registered, computed from the next local pointer against the synchronized remote pointer
key_decisions.plan_choice: Registered flags from the next pointer vs the synchronized pointer (Cummings style)

key_decisions.ma_choice: Full = next wgray equals synced rgray with the two MSBs inverted; empty = Gray equality
key_decisions.plan_choice: Gray compare with the top two bits inverted for full; equality for empty

key_decisions.ma_choice: Occupancy levels (level >= AF_LEVEL, level <= AE_LEVEL) from gray2bin of the synced pointer, using the next local pointer
key_decisions.plan_choice: Occupancy-level thresholds; Gray-to-binary of the synced pointer for the fill level
key_decisions.note: Neither the MA nor the plan specified default threshold values. The MA uses DEPTH-4 and 4; the plan leaves this open.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Coupled async clear wrst_n & rrst_n into both domains; either reset flushes the FIFO; each side releases synchronously after both deassert
key_decisions.plan_choice: Coupled flush with the combined async clear and per-domain release after both resets deassert (from the Q1 answer)

key_decisions.ma_choice: Per-domain rst_sync (async assert, sync deassert); the write side stays in reset if wclk is stopped at release
key_decisions.plan_choice: An internal async-assert/sync-deassert reset synchronizer per domain; the stopped-wclk case is covered explicitly

key_decisions.ma_choice: Flop/LUT-RAM array, synchronous write on wclk, asynchronous read captured into rd_data_q on rclk, no reset; RAM macro for large DEPTH
key_decisions.plan_choice: Flop array with combinational read into a registered rd_data, wrapped so a macro can be swapped in
key_decisions.note: The plan leaves memory reset as a question to answer later. The MA explicitly does not reset the array.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Dedicated sync_ff module parameterized by SYNC_STAGES (default 2), ASYNC_REG attributes
key_decisions.plan_choice: Dedicated parameterized sync module (SYNC_STAGES=2) with ASYNC_REG/dont_touch attributes

key_decisions.ma_choice: Ignore wr_en when full and rd_en when empty; no error flags
key_decisions.plan_choice: Ignore writes and reads at the boundaries; SVA only; no extra error ports

key_decisions.ma_choice: Adds a convenience rd_valid output that pulses one cycle after an accepted read
key_decisions.plan_choice: Keeps strictly to the spec port list; no rd_valid
key_decisions.note: This adds an output port the plan does not have, so the interface changes.

key_decisions.ma_choice: set_clock_groups -asynchronous, plus set_max_delay -datapath_only 5 ns and set_bus_skew on the Gray buses and the memory read path
key_decisions.plan_choice: No asynchronous clock group or blanket false path; set_max_delay -datapath_only 5 ns plus a bus-skew limit on the Gray buses and the mem-to-rd_data path
key_decisions.note: The RTL is unchanged. The plan avoids the clock-group/max_delay precedence pitfall, which arguably makes it the cleaner choice.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Treated as pointer-qualified; SpyGlass FIFO declaration waives Ac_unsync02; path bounded to one rclk period
key_decisions.plan_choice: Memory crossing recognized as FIFO-qualified in SpyGlass; max_delay 5 ns on the mem-to-rd_data path

key_decisions.decision: Behaviour when wclk stops with buffered data
key_decisions.ma_choice: The reader keeps sampling the stable wgray and drains every accepted word
key_decisions.plan_choice: All words written before the stop remain readable; wr_full may be stale but is pessimistic

key_decisions.ma_choice: rd_empty=1, rd_almost_empty=1, wr_full=0, wr_almost_full=0 out of reset
key_decisions.note: The plan only says reset values must be 'chosen so no flag is optimistic' and leaves wr_full's value unresolved. That wording could even imply wr_full=1 during reset.

summary: The plan closely tracks the reference MA. Its Gray pointer and flag scheme, registered next-pointer flags, occupancy-level almost flags, coupled async-clear reset with per-domain synchronizers, flop-array storage and sync module all match, as does its stopped-clock and overflow handling. It differs in two places. It does not add the MA's convenience rd_valid port, which is an interface difference. Its SDC avoids set_clock_groups -asynchronous in favour of max_delay plus bus_skew only, which is equivalent and arguably cleaner. Flag reset values are left unresolved. Q1 was a legitimate question. Q2 (target format) was answered with the default and did not affect the architecture.
